text:
Emma: Quick sync — we need to lock priorities for the model registry roadmap for Q2. Customers (FinPlus, Acme) asked for smoother migrations and clearer pin-exception behavior. Can we agree top 3 deliverables: onboarding checklist + baseline bench, pin-exception SLA + escalation, and a migration assist path (compat shims)? Tagging @Ravi @Sofia @Tomas @Maya for cost/tech/comm tradeoffs. ETA for a proposal by EOD Fri?

Ravi: Can you clarify the "baseline bench" — sample sizes, metrics, and where it runs? :thinking:

Emma: Bench slice = representative slices for gen vs embeds. Target ~1k samples per tenant as a baseline for manual runs; metrics: p95 latency, 99th token latency, quality regression rate. MVP: manual bench step triggered during onboarding PR; auto-bench later.

Sofia: 1k/tenant is pretty heavy for auto runs. Suggest stratified 200 samples + focused stress tests for infra/perf. For quality regressions we need an eval harness — that'll take ~2-3 sprints to bake in if we want automated gating.

Tomas: Routing/ops note: pin-exception support implies changes to routing layer (special-cased variant routing). We'll need a fallback policy and canary window. Plan: add a "pin-exception" flag with explicit fallback target + per-version traces. Canary = 2 weeks recommended.

Maya: From CS: major customers want an opt-out/migration credit path and a clearly documented rollback. A 30-day "escape hatch" after migration reduces churn. Also they'll ask for a playbook we can hand them.

Ravi: Cost rough numbers — manual bench + storage for samples is cheap; auto-bench + harness + orchestration is ~ $2-3k/month per 100 models initially (depends on sampling). We can reduce by sampling and quantized test runs. Need product to show these deltas in UI.

Emma: Proposal for MVP timeline:
- Sprint A: onboarding checklist + manual bench run + onboarding doc (low effort)
- Sprint B: auto-bench (stratified 200 samples), basic eval harness, and model metadata schema (seq_len_dist, tokenizer_hash)
- Sprint C: pin-exception flow + 30d escape hatch + canary rollout + observability (per-version p95/p99, error-rate)
Owners: @Ravi infra, @Sofia evals, @Tomas routing/ops, @Maya comms/customer playbook.

Ravi: I'll own infra. I'll sketch the config model and cost estimate by Thu. Will include a minimal "estimate endpoint" for per-model onboarding cost.

Sofia: I'll prototype the eval harness and sampling script. Heads-up: we need explicit model metadata fields on ingest (seq_len_dist, tokenization id, tokenizer_hash) or sampling will be unreliable.

Tomas: I'll add routing flags and fallback policy to the canary playbook. Also need traces/metrics: per-version token-cost delta and per-version error-rate.

Maya: I'll draft customer-facing playbook + slide pack and a short console copy for the opt-in checkbox. Low-effort: place a single checkbox "Show estimated cost and opt into auto-bench" during onboarding.

InfraBot: Created ticket: https://redwood.internal/infra/REG-2145 "registry auto-bench MVP" — assigned to Ravi, due 2024-04-18

Emma: One last Q: should we surface a rough cost estimate in the console before onboarding? I think that reduces surprise.

Ravi: Yes, adding a lightweight estimate endpoint is straight-forward. I'll include a short delta summary (expected token-cost change, estimated infra run time) on the model page.

Emma: Great. We'll reconvene Fri 10am to finalize tradeoffs and sign-off. Thanks all :thumbsup:
